examBlueprint.title: Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline - July 2026
examBlueprint.role: Controls the domains, task coverage, domain weights, eligibility information, exam structure, and the professional responsibilities assessed on the PMP examination.

primaryKnowledgeSpine.title: A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide) - Eighth Edition and The Standard for Project Management
primaryKnowledgeSpine.role: Provides the primary principles, performance-domain knowledge, value-delivery orientation, tailoring logic, and evolved process guidance used to explain why strong project decisions work.

companionReferences.title: Agile Practice Guide
companionReferences.role: Supports adaptive and agile ways of working, team practices, iterative planning, feedback, and value delivery.

companionReferences.title: Process Groups: A Practice Guide
companionReferences.role: Supports predictive delivery through initiating, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, and closing, including process interactions and associated project-management practices.

teachingRule: Every exam objective is taught through an ECO task, a PMBOK principle or performance domain, an appropriate predictive, adaptive, or hybrid way of working, an original business scenario, a practical artifact, and original exam-style practice. The course does not treat the PMBOK Guide as a question bank and does not assume memorization alone is sufficient.

principles.label: Holistic project view
principles.courseApplication: Evaluate the project as part of an organizational, stakeholder, product, operational, financial, regulatory, and environmental system rather than as an isolated schedule.

principles.label: Value and outcome focus
principles.courseApplication: Prioritize outcomes and benefits that are worth the effort and expense, not delivery activity alone.

principles.label: Quality embedded in delivery
principles.courseApplication: Build quality, acceptance, regulatory, assurance, and improvement practices into the work rather than relying only on final inspection.

principles.label: Accountable leadership
principles.courseApplication: Exercise ethical judgment, transparent communication, appropriate authority, and responsibility for project decisions and consequences.

principles.label: Sustainability integration
principles.courseApplication: Consider environmental, social, economic, operational, and long-term impacts when planning and evaluating project decisions.

principles.label: Empowered teams
principles.courseApplication: Create clear purpose, trust, decision boundaries, collaboration, learning, and appropriate autonomy.

performanceDomains.label: Governance
performanceDomains.courseApplication: Decision rights, policies, ethics, oversight, success measures, escalation, compliance, and change authority.

performanceDomains.label: Scope
performanceDomains.courseApplication: Requirements, deliverables, boundaries, decomposition, backlogs, acceptance, and scope-change integrity.

performanceDomains.label: Schedule
performanceDomains.courseApplication: Sequencing, dependencies, estimation, critical path, adaptive forecasting, baselines, variation, and recovery.

performanceDomains.label: Finance
performanceDomains.courseApplication: Funding needs, estimates, budgets, contingency, reserves, reporting, forecasts, and value-based financial decisions.

performanceDomains.label: Stakeholders
performanceDomains.courseApplication: Identification, analysis, engagement, expectations, customer value, communication, trust, and influence.

performanceDomains.label: Resources
performanceDomains.courseApplication: People, capability, equipment, services, suppliers, capacity, availability, optimization, and accountability.

performanceDomains.label: Risk
performanceDomains.courseApplication: Threats, opportunities, assumptions, uncertainty, analysis, responses, reserves, issues, and residual exposure.

courseModuleCrosswalk.examPurpose: Establish the ECO, PMBOK knowledge architecture, ethics, exam expectations, and predictive-adaptive-hybrid reasoning model.
Prepare learners for vision, leadership, roles, team empowerment, diverse perspectives, problem solving, and performance scenarios.
Prepare learners for stakeholder engagement, expectation alignment, conflict, communication, reporting, trust, influence, and knowledge transfer.
Prepare learners to tailor delivery, integrate plans, define scope, prioritize value, estimate work, analyze dependencies, and use data.
Prepare learners for resource planning, procurement, negotiation, contracts, supplier performance, project finance, quality, compliance, and improvement.
Prepare learners for schedule development and control, status evaluation, artifacts, forecasts, communication, acceptance, transition, and closure.
Prepare learners for governance, success metrics, compliance, change control, organizational change, and external business conditions.
Prepare learners for risk, issues, impediments, improvement, organizational learning, AI, sustainability, and integrated exam readiness.

sequence: Identify the ECO task and professional responsibility being tested.
Explain the associated PMBOK principle and performance-domain knowledge.
Compare predictive, adaptive or agile, and hybrid application.
Analyze facts, assumptions, uncertainty, authority, value, and stakeholder consequences.
Use an original project scenario and produce a practical business artifact.
Complete original exam-style practice and explain every distractor.
Use the AI tutor for remediation outside protected graded-assessment mode.
instructionalMethod.memorizationPolicy: Terminology, formulas, and process relationships are taught where useful, but scenario judgment and application are prioritized because the exam evaluates critical thinking in realistic situations.
instructionalMethod.examIntegrityPolicy: No recalled examination items, exam dumps, protected test content, PMI official question banks, or misleading claims of actual exam questions are permitted.

rightsAndLicensing.learnerAccessRequirement: Learners should obtain lawful access to the current PMBOK Guide and any companion PMI publications assigned for reading. Separate PMI membership or purchase may be required.
rightsAndLicensing.obserraUsage: Obserra instruction, examples, diagrams, practice questions, and explanations must be original. PMI publications are cited and paraphrased within applicable permission and copyright limits.
prohibited: copying substantial PMBOK text, figures, tables, process descriptions, or official courseware without permission
using PMI logos or suggesting sponsorship, endorsement, authorization, or ATP status
representing Obserra original questions as real PMP exam questions
rightsAndLicensing.publicationGate: Legal, copyright, trademark, subject-matter, and exam-integrity review must confirm the current editions and permitted use before public release.
